title: Single-cell analysis of neuroimmune signatures of pain
summary: scRNA-seq analysis for a study mapping immune-cell programs and neuroimmune interactions across three inflammatory pain models.
problem: Inflammatory pain involves diverse immune and sensory-neuron populations whose changing cellular states and interactions are difficult to resolve with bulk measurements.
approach: Ashish Jain carried out the scRNA-seq data analysis, including quality control, integration, clustering, cell-type annotation, and downstream comparisons. The custom CellChat interaction database used by the study was generated by collaborators and was not part of his contribution.
outcomes: Resolved immune-cell populations across zymosan, incision, and ultraviolet-burn pain models
Characterized cell-type-specific transcriptional programs associated with pain and resolution
Supported analysis of injury-specific neuroimmune interaction patterns
Delivered reproducible results and publication-ready visualizations

title: Ancestry-stratified GWAS of strabismus
summary: Genome-wide association analysis of strabismus using whole-genome sequencing and clinical data from the All of Us Research Program.
problem: Although strabismus has a substantial genetic component, its risk loci and the extent to which associations differ among ancestry groups have remained incompletely understood.
approach: Ashish Jain carried out the GWAS analysis, including ancestry-aware cohort preparation, genotype and phenotype quality control, covariate-adjusted association testing, and interpretation of ancestry-specific results.
outcomes: Analyzed European, Admixed American, and African American ancestry cohorts separately
Identified significant loci in the African American and Admixed American cohorts
Produced Manhattan plots and analysis-ready association results
Demonstrated the importance of diverse cohorts in strabismus genetics

title: Proteomics analysis in ophthalmology research
summary: Proteomics data analysis supporting an ophthalmology study published through Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science.
problem: High-dimensional proteomics studies require careful assay quality control, statistical modeling, and biological interpretation to distinguish reproducible protein signals from technical variation.
approach: Ashish Jain carried out the proteomics analysis, including data quality assessment, normalization review, differential protein analysis, pathway-level interpretation, and preparation of publication-ready results.
outcomes: Established an analysis-ready proteomics dataset
Identified proteins showing study-relevant abundance differences
Connected protein-level signals to biological pathways
Generated clear figures and statistical summaries for scientific communication

title: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of early intestinal failure-associated liver disease
summary: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of liver tissue in a preterm piglet model used to investigate the early mechanisms of intestinal failure-associated liver disease.
problem: Children receiving long-term parenteral nutrition can develop intestinal failure-associated liver disease, but the molecular processes driving its earliest stages remain poorly understood.
approach: Ashish Jain carried out the bulk RNA-seq data analysis, including sequencing quality control, alignment and quantification, sample-level diagnostics, differential expression testing, and pathway-enrichment analysis comparing parenteral-nutrition and bottle-fed groups.
outcomes: Detected broad transcriptomic differences between parenteral-nutrition and control liver tissue
Identified 2,060 differentially expressed genes after quality control and statistical testing
Revealed activation of inflammatory pathways and inhibition of cell-cycle and metabolic programs
Supported prioritization of potential therapeutic strategies that may counteract disease-associated gene dysregulation

title: MAFDash
summary: A dashboard builder that makes mutation annotation format data easier to explore and share.
problem: Mutation datasets can be technically dense and difficult for multidisciplinary teams to interrogate together.
approach: MAFDash turns curated mutation data into interactive views that support cohort exploration, gene-level review, and clearer research communication.
outcomes: Interactive cohort exploration
Shareable visual summaries
Open-source implementation
Designed for non-programmatic users
